title: Naruto Mobile finally gets a global release after a decade in China
summary: Saturday was Naruto Uzumaki’s birthday, which also happened to be the day his mobile fighter got its passport sorted. Naruto Mobile, the MoreFun Studios fighting game that’s been running in China since 2016, is getting a global release on iOS and Android, with Bandai Namco bringing it over. A decade is a fairly long time for an import. It launched in mainland China in May 2016 and has done very well for itself there since, while the rest of us looked on from outside. I’ve had takeaway orders take a scenic route before, but nothing like that. ... [MORE]

title: Brotato's Primal Dread DLC now has a release date, but you'll be waiting a bit for mobile
summary: It seems like it's been months since we heard about Brotato's latest DLC, Primal Dread. And that's because it was last heard being announced all the way back in April of this year. But, fortunately, we now have a release date, although you'll still be waiting a while for it on mobile! While it may be a bit of a wait, Brotato's Primal Dread DLC comes jam-packed with new content to enjoy. There's a host of new weapons and characters, as well as a massive primordial-themed map to explore and bosses to challenge, including a skyscraper-sized kaiju that you can only see the legs of! It's certainly got size going for it, if nothing else. ... [MORE]

title: Replaced sees the dystopic cyberpunk platformer making its way to Android
summary: It's a bit of a trite observation, but sometimes it really feels as if we're living in a cyberpunk dystopia, just without the cool stuff. Fortunately, if you're hankering for a neon-soaked world to explore, then you're in luck, because 2.5D cinematic platformer Replaced is set to make its way to Android on December 9th! Set in an alternate-universe 1980s America, you play as R.E.A.C.H., an AI that's been unexpectedly placed into a human body. You'll explore the sprawling metropolis of Phoenix City and do battle with the sinister Phoenix Corporation in your typical dour cyberpunk urban hellscape where human life is cheap. ... [MORE]

summary: Azur Promilia, the upcoming fantasy ARPG from developer Manjuu Games, is set to launch its first English-language beta in summer 2027, it has been announced. The news comes alongside a massive 20-million pre-registration milestone and their first English promo video. Azur Promilia is set in a fantasy world populated by both humans and creatures called Kibo. Alongside the usual fantasy ARPG adventure, you'll also be able to befriend and recruit Kibos, using their distinctive abilities to help you out in both exploration and combat. All this, and both the distinctive anime-inspired character designs that Manjuu are well known for. ... [MORE]

title: ReStory, the electronics repair sim, is making its way to Android and iOS
summary: If you're a fan of retro gaming, repairing electronics and Y2K aesthetics, then you're in for a treat. ReStory: Chill Repair Shop from developer Mandragora is set to make its way to iOS and Android. With pre-registration now open on Google Play and a planned iOS App Store release, it brings the joy of repair to your smartphone. ReStory has you take on the role of an electronics repair shop owner in mid-2000s Tokyo. Your job is, of course, to repair electronics, ranging from laptops to handheld game consoles and beyond. That means doing everything from disassembling them, cleaning them, and even hunting down spare parts when your own library of replacements isn't up to scratch. ... [MORE]

title: The One Bullet Job is a heist puzzler where you only get one shot. Literally.
summary: We all love a good heist film, like Ocean's Eleven or Mission: Impossible. But translating that into a game has proven surprisingly tricky, even as it's been attempted as far back as the days of tabletop gaming. Now, The One Bullet Job is the latest to try and make you feel like a master thief when it arrives on Android October 16th. If you hadn't already guessed, One Bullet Job's core gimmick is right in the title. You play a heister whose objective is to navigate the grid, gather cash, avoid guards, and, if necessary, take them out before making your escape. And, of course, you have only one bullet to do so. ... [MORE]

title: Ink Parry: Seonbi Swordsman sees you take on the challenge of conducting the perfect parry
summary: The perfect parry is something entire games, such as Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice, are built around. There's something thrilling about not just avoiding an enemy's attack, but negating it entirely, and it's that exact feeling that Ink Parry: Seonbi Swordsman is looking to replicate on iOS and Android, on sale now! The gameplay of Ink Parry: Seonbi Swordsman is deceptively simple. Your hero sits at the centre of the screen, as attacks fly towards him and are parried depending on how you move your hand. Cut arrows mid-flight, catch maces and tear open nets as you build up some truly dizzying combos of perfect parries. ... [MORE]

title: Orion Backgammon lets you check whether the dice really are playing fair
summary: Anyone who has played backgammon online for long enough has accused the dice of something. Usually out loud, usually to nobody. Orion Backgammon has just arrived on iPhone and iPad after launching on Android in August, and the independent studio behind it, Arthea, has actually done something about it. Its dice are provably fair. Before a match starts, the seed that decides every roll is sealed away, and once it ends your own phone checks that nothing was swapped along the way. Think of it as writing your prediction on a card and putting it in an envelope before the match.  ... [MORE]

title: Door Kickers 2 brings tense tactical action to get your blood pumping on Android
summary: Ever since the first Modern Warfare introduced a generation of kids to the SAS, tactical warfare has become a surprisingly prominent niche. No strafing or bunny hopping here, just slow, methodical room clearing. And if you're looking to have that particular itch scratched on mobile, then Door Kickers 2 is for you! Now available for pre-registration on Android, Door Kickers 2 is an innovative strategy game that has you controlling a small squad of operators stationed in the country of Nowheraki. You direct them from a top-down perspective, choosing all their moves while being able to pause the game at any time and readjust. The only rule? No take-backs, and it'll require innovative thinking to predict where and when your enemy will pop up. ... [MORE]

Naruto Mobile, the MoreFun Studios fighting game that’s been running in China since 2016, is getting a global release on iOS and Android, with Bandai Namco bringing it over. title: Replaced sees the dystopic cyberpunk platformer making its way to Android
summary: It's a bit of a trite observation, but sometimes it really feels as if we're living in a cyberpunk dystopia, just without the cool stuff. Fortunately, if you're hankering for a neon-soaked world to explore, then you're in luck, because 2.5D cinematic platformer Replaced is set to make its way to Android on December 9th! Set in an alternate-universe 1980s America, you play as R.E.A.C.H., an AI that's been unexpectedly placed into a human body. You'll explore the sprawling metropolis of Phoenix City and do battle with the sinister Phoenix Corporation in your typical dour cyberpunk urban hellscape where human life is cheap. ... [MORE]

summary: If you're a fan of retro gaming, repairing electronics and Y2K aesthetics, then you're in for a treat. ReStory: Chill Repair Shop from developer Mandragora is set to make its way to iOS and Android. With pre-registration now open on Google Play and a planned iOS App Store release, it brings the joy of repair to your smartphone. ReStory has you take on the role of an electronics repair shop owner in mid-2000s Tokyo. Your job is, of course, to repair electronics, ranging from laptops to handheld game consoles and beyond. That means doing everything from disassembling them, cleaning them, and even hunting down spare parts when your own library of replacements isn't up to scratch. ... [MORE]

title: The One Bullet Job is a heist puzzler where you only get one shot. Literally.
summary: We all love a good heist film, like Ocean's Eleven or Mission: Impossible. But translating that into a game has proven surprisingly tricky, even as it's been attempted as far back as the days of tabletop gaming. Now, The One Bullet Job is the latest to try and make you feel like a master thief when it arrives on Android October 16th. If you hadn't already guessed, One Bullet Job's core gimmick is right in the title. You play a heister whose objective is to navigate the grid, gather cash, avoid guards, and, if necessary, take them out before making your escape. And, of course, you have only one bullet to do so. ... [MORE]

title: Ink Parry: Seonbi Swordsman sees you take on the challenge of conducting the perfect parry
summary: The perfect parry is something entire games, such as Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice, are built around. There's something thrilling about not just avoiding an enemy's attack, but negating it entirely, and it's that exact feeling that Ink Parry: Seonbi Swordsman is looking to replicate on iOS and Android, on sale now! title: Orion Backgammon lets you check whether the dice really are playing fair
summary: Anyone who has played backgammon online for long enough has accused the dice of something. Usually out loud, usually to nobody. Orion Backgammon has just arrived on iPhone and iPad after launching on Android in August, and the independent studio behind it, Arthea, has actually done something about it. Its dice are provably fair. Before a match starts, the seed that decides every roll is sealed away, and once it ends your own phone checks that nothing was swapped along the way. Think of it as writing your prediction on a card and putting it in an envelope before the match.  ... [MORE]

title: Door Kickers 2 brings tense tactical action to get your blood pumping on Android
summary: Ever since the first Modern Warfare introduced a generation of kids to the SAS, tactical warfare has become a surprisingly prominent niche. No strafing or bunny hopping here, just slow, methodical room clearing. And if you're looking to have that particular itch scratched on mobile, then Door Kickers 2 is for you! No take-backs, and it'll require innovative thinking to predict where and when your enemy will pop up. ... [MORE]
